key_insight: HVAF-sprayed Tribaloy-400 formed a denser, more protective oxide layer than DS, giving better resistance to molten solar-salt corrosion at 500 °C.
engineering_relevance: For concentrating solar power thermal-storage containers, HVAF appears to be the more reliable coating route for extending service life under long-duration nitrate-salt exposure.
method: Tribaloy-400 coatings were deposited on ASTM A516 steel by HVAF and detonation spraying.
Specimens were exposed to 60% NaNO3–40% KNO3 molten salt at 500 °C for up to 1000 h.
Microstructure, phase formation, and elemental penetration were assessed by SEM, mapping, and phase analysis.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that HVAF maintained a uniform Cr–Mo–Si–O enriched surface with minimal salt penetration after 1000 h, while DS showed deeper ingress, higher mass gain, and more spallation.
watch_item: Results are tied to a specific salt chemistry, temperature, and substrate, so coating selection may change under different CSP operating conditions.
paper_title: Hot corrosion behavior of thermal sprayed using HVAF and DS techniques with Tribaloy-400 coatings for solar energy storage container
